test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Whom does the Census 2011 identify as a literate person?

options.text: A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language
A person aged 5 years and above who can read and write in any of the languages listed in the 8th schedule of the constitution
A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write and solve basic arithmetic problems
A person who can read his/her name and address in any language

solution:
The correct answer is __**A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language** is identified as a literate person by Census 2011.
 
• The literacy criteria focus on the ability to read and write with comprehension in any language, emphasizing understanding rather than merely the ability to read and write.
 
• This definition helps in assessing the educational development and literacy rate of the population accurately.
 
• The age threshold of 7 years is set to ensure that the data reflects a more accurate representation of literacy, as children below this age are generally not expected to have developed reading and writing skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011** is the 15th National Census of India, conducted by the Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The census collects various demographic data, including population count, literacy rate, employment status, and housing conditions.
 
• It plays a crucial role in policy-making, planning, and administration by providing accurate and comprehensive data about the country's population.
 
• The literacy rate is a key indicator of educational attainment and is used to measure the progress and effectiveness of educational policies and programs.
 
• Efforts to improve literacy rates include government initiatives like the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and the National Literacy Mission (NLM).
